c1-37.title: A Weekend of Finals
c1-37.story: Max called it the busiest sports weekend of his life. On Saturday morning he sat in the stands for the city [[derby]]. His cousin's team was losing until their [[winger]] slipped past two defenders and scored in the final minute. That afternoon he dragged Anna to a cricket match at the university. Neither of them really understood the rules, but they cheered whenever the [[bowler]] sent the wickets flying. In the evening they watched a tennis final on TV, and a young player won her first [[grand slam]] after nearly three hours. On Sunday Max wanted to follow the [[grand prix]], but Anna had already booked something calmer. They rented a small [[fiberglass]] boat on the Dnipro, and Max spent the whole hour checking the race on his phone. By the time he looked up, Anna had rowed them back to shore by herself. "Next weekend," she said, "we're doing absolutely nothing."

c1-38.title: Game Night at Grandma's
c1-38.story: Every Friday Anna's grandparents host a game night, and this week Lisa and Ira joined them. Grandma started with [[mahjong]], which she plays so quickly that the girls could barely follow the tiles. Later Grandpa brought out a deck of cards and a bowl of sunflower seeds to use instead of chips. Ira, who is usually shy, pushed her whole pile forward and announced that she was going [[all-in]]. Everyone assumed it was a [[bluff]], so Grandpa called, only to watch her lay down a [[full house]]. "You're a born [[gambler]]," he groaned, although everyone knew she had never played before. Lisa joked that Ira was a secret [[hustler]] who had only been pretending to be a beginner. To calm things down, Taras persuaded them to try his fantasy board game, but his wizard ran out of [[mana]] in the second round. Grandpa, still sulking about the cards, played the [[endgame]] with surprising patience and won the whole thing. "Some of us," he said with a wink, "just need time to warm up."

c1-39.title: A Night of Dancing
c1-39.story: For her grandparents' fortieth anniversary, Anna offered to be the DJ, which turned out to be harder than she expected. Every generation in the room seemed to want a completely different kind of music. Grandma requested a [[polka]], and to everyone's surprise Grandpa spun her around the floor like a young man. Then Anna's dad asked for [[hard rock]], insisting it was what he had played at his own wedding. Sofia wanted something calmer, so Anna tried a little [[new age]], but the room went so quiet that she quickly switched to eighties [[new wave]]. Max, who had come along to help, kept begging for [[electro]] and a few old [[acid house]] tracks, claiming the party needed the energy of a [[rave]]. Mama laughed and said she hadn't been to one of those in twenty years. In the end, Anna found a playlist of [[world music]] that mixed rhythms from every continent, and suddenly everyone was dancing together. Grandpa taught Lisa the [[mambo]], while Taras invented his own wild version of the [[boogie]]. By midnight, even Sofia admitted it had been the best party in years.

c1-40.title: Band Rehearsal
c1-40.story: Max's school band had only one week left before the spring concert, and Tuesday's rehearsal was a mess. Sofia, who plays [[synth]], kept arriving late because of her chemistry club. Their new drummer hadn't learned the songs yet, so a friend filled in on [[bongos|bongo]], which gave everything an unexpected beach feeling. Max struggled with the long [[instrumental]] in the middle of the second song, and his [[sax]] solo kept falling apart. Lisa played the [[piccolo]] part perfectly but looked bored waiting for the others to catch up. Then Ira arrived to take over lead [[vocals|vocal]], and something finally clicked. Halfway through the chorus, the band settled into a relaxed [[groove]] that none of them wanted to stop. When the music teacher struck the old [[gong]] in the corner to end the session, they all groaned in disappointment. For the first time that month, they actually felt ready.

c1-41.title: The First Album
c1-41.story: Max and his friends had been talking about making an album for months, and this summer they finally did it. They began by recording a rough [[demo]] in Max's garage, with egg cartons taped to the walls to soften the sound. Max, who had become the band's [[frontman]] almost by accident, wrote most of the lyrics himself. Their first gig at a local café was a complete [[fiasco]]. The power went out during the second song, and the owner had to restart the old [[jukebox]] to keep the customers happy. Still, they refused to give up. By August their [[debut]] was ready: eight songs inspired by the seventies rock [[revival]] that Max's dad loved. The [[title track]], a song about the Kyiv metro at night, quickly became a favorite among their classmates. Taras proudly called himself the band's first [[groupie]] and followed them to every rehearsal with a homemade sign. When the album reached a thousand plays online, Sofia declared it a [[mega]] success, and they celebrated with pizza on the garage floor.

c1-42.title: Opera Night
c1-42.story: For her birthday, Anna's grandmother wanted only one thing: an evening at the opera with the whole family. Taras complained all the way there, convinced he would fall asleep in the first ten minutes. Before the curtain rose, a string [[quartet]] played in the foyer, and he stopped to watch the cellist with genuine curiosity. The opera itself opened with the chorus singing in [[unison]], so powerfully that the floor seemed to tremble. In the second act, the leading [[soprano]] performed a long [[aria]] that left Grandma wiping her eyes. Afterward the whole [[ensemble]] came out to take a bow, and the audience rose to applaud. On the tram home, Taras tried to impress everyone by singing a scale, but he got stuck after mi because he couldn't remember [[fa]]. Anna whispered it to him, and he finished proudly on a very high [[la]] that made the other passengers smile. Grandma said it was the best birthday present she had ever received.

c1-43.title: The Old Theater Reopens
c1-43.story: An old theater near Anna's university had been closed for years, and this fall it finally reopened. Workers spent months repairing the [[exterior]], and the cracked stone [[facade]] now looks almost new. Anna and Lisa went on the opening weekend, which felt more like a festival than a single show. On Friday there was a [[cabaret]] with songs, jokes, and a pianist in a top hat. On Saturday a local company staged a [[farce]] about two brothers who keep swapping places, and the audience laughed until they cried. The host that evening was a [[drag queen]] in a glittering gown, who welcomed everyone with warm, quick-witted jokes. Sunday afternoon was devoted to [[improv]], and Lisa was pulled on stage to play a confused tourist. The weekend ended with a [[masquerade]], and the girls wore paper masks they had made themselves. On the way out, Anna noticed an old poster in the lobby showing that the building had been a [[music hall]] more than a century ago. "Some places," Lisa said, "are simply made for entertainment."

c1-44.title: At the Art Gallery
c1-44.story: For a school project, Anna and Max had to visit an exhibition and compare two different styles of painting. They chose a small [[art space]] in a former factory near the river, which was hosting a show about five centuries of European art. The first room was devoted to the [[Renaissance|renaissance]], and Anna stood for a long time in front of a gentle [[Madonna|madonna]] holding a sleeping child. Max preferred the next hall, where the artists of the early twentieth-century [[avant-garde]] seemed to have broken every rule they could find. Their guide explained how the careful [[realism]] of earlier painters had given way to bold colors and strange shapes. She also pointed out the hidden [[symbolism]] in one canvas, where a melting candle stood for lost time. In a short workshop, they were asked to draw the [[contour]] of a face in a single line, which was much harder than it looked. Outside, the factory walls were covered in [[public art]] by local teenagers. Anna photographed one mural to use as the main [[visual]] for their presentation, and their teacher later called it the most original project in the class.
